div.p: HIGHWAY' MATTERS.

In response to a memorial,. the Highway Committee rescinded their resolution to macadam Church-se., Palm- worth, and resolved to repair the present boulder pave- ment. The Committee recommended that the following tenders be accepted subject to the sanction of the Local Government Board to the borrowing of the money and to the usual conditions, viz. :—Contract No. 1; streets and back passages at MOSS Bank, Messrs. Cowburn and Sons £3,328 125.; No. 2, Thomas-st., Guest-st., Post Office place, &a., Messrs Cowburn and Son £1;994 155.; No. 3, East-st., Edward-st., &c., Messrs. Son, and Sons, £836 16s. ; No. 4, brick sewer, Lowerhouse-lane, Messrs. Sayce and Randle £2,062 154. id. The Surveyor was instrncted to take proceedings to have the property in Victoria-st., belonging to the Prescot Building Society, declared dangerous buildings.—Arrangements had been . made with Major Cross, representing Hutchinson' trim- 'tees, for flushing the marsh outfall sewer.—The minutes were passed without discussion on the motion of Mt. ;Taylor.

div.head: 171 E. HEALTH. OF THE TOWN.
div.p: 171 E. HEALTH. OF THE TOWN.

The minutes of the Health Committee recorded a gift of fruit to the hospitals by Mr. J. S. Gilliat, M.P. .for which he was thanked. There were three patients in the Accident Hospital. and nine in the Infectious Dis- eases Hospital. The medical officer reported that during September there were 104 births and 66 deaths being at the respective rates of 416 and 26.4. There were 37 deaths amongst children under five years: There were eight inquests. The notifications of ' in- fectious diseases were as follow :—Enteric or typhoid fever 34, erysipelas 6, membranous croup 2, scarlet fever 9, total 51. The medical officer continued: The death rate is high this month, but if the deaths of children tinder 1 year old and of those between 1 and 5 years of age, and also the number of inquests be sub- tracted from the total, there would be left a death rate of about 9 per 1,000 of the population over 5 years of age:—When calling your attention to the village of Appleton in my last report I omitted to refer to the very unsanitary condition of Tithebarn-street, where a few miserable drainage pipes are on the surface, broken here and there, and blocked up with refuse. There are some houses in this Btre3t that have neither backyards nor backdoors and the inhabitants are compelled to empty, their slops through the front door. It would he well if this state of things could be remedied.—The pits in Widnes-road and Albert-road, which I called your atten- tion to in last month's report, have not yet been attended to.-1 would respectfully call the attention of the Health Committee to the great increase of the number of cases of smallpox, which are taking place in Warrington, between which town and ours there is such constant intercourse, in order that ample provision should be made to meet it sh.uld it come amongst us.— - It as been found necessary to destroy some bedding in a house in Warrington-road, where a death took place from typhoid fever, and which was duly attended to by the Sanitary Inspector. Mr Wright in moving the confirmation of the minntes, said typhoid fever was prevalent but the Inc heal officer said there was nothing extra. There had been an exti a staff of men engaged to deal with nightsoil, and disin- fectants were being freely used in all parts of the town. With a smallpox epidemic raging at Warrington they had every reason to be thankful that they stood in the position they did, and the Committee had made arrange- ments for dealing with an outbreak should it unfortu- nately occur.—Mr. Cook seconded the motion, and pointed out many cases of fever had occurred in Elliot and Gladstone-streets, and it was imperative that they should be made at once.—Mr. Beech said the property owners in those streets were anxious to keep their pro- perty in a sanitary condition, and he thought Mr. Cook's remarks uncalled for—Mr. Taylor said there were.no drains in those streets ; the Highway Committee would see that something was done at once.—Mr. Beeclo, charged the nightsoil men with not carrying out the work properly, and with placing rubbish on a piece oi waste land.—Mr. Wright denied both accusations, and said the Board did not get the assistance from property? owners in keeping the town in a sanitary condition that, they should.—The minutes wore adopted.

div.head: PROPOSED VEHICULAR BRIDGE.
div.p: THE PROPOSED VEHICULAR BRIDGE.

. . The General Purposes Committee reported that depu- tations from the Runcorn Improvement Commissioners and the Runcorn Rural Sanitary Authority attended, the Commissioners being represented by Messrs. Wiswall, Lightburn, Fisher and the Law Clerk, and the Rural Sanitary Authority by Messrs. Heywood, Aaron, Bran- dreth, and the clerk (Mr. Ashton). The matter of the bridge was further discussed and an arrangement for concerted action in the terms of the following resolution was agreed to. The deputations then withdrew and it was moved by Mr. Brown, seconded by Mr. Sadler, and carried unanimously, that the Committee having given the question of the construction of a bridge f.r vehicular and other traffic over the river Mersey between Widnes and Runcorn very full consideration, and the Clerk having reported the result of the meeting between the committees of the County Councils of Lancashire and Cheshire appointed to enquire as to the necessity for the proposed bridge held on the 25th May last, and the Cern- mittee having also had an opportunity of ascertaining the views of representatives of the Runcorn Impreve- ment.Commissioners upon the subject, resolve that it is desirable in the interests of the district of Whines and the surrounding neig,libdurhood, that the most effitaci- ous steps should be taken to procure the construction of f uch a bridge at the earliest opportunity. And also that sunject to the fulfillment of the following conditions, , Viz: (a) Authority to levy tolls for the use of the bridge for such a period as may be necessary for the purpose next hereinafter mentioned. (b) The constitution of such tolls as a first charge to secure repayment of the 'contributions hereinafter mentioned. (c) The creation of such rating areas as may hereafter be decided upon and agreed to, and (d) the contribution of a like amount '1 as that next hereinafter mentioned by the Runcorn Im- provement Commissioners. And in order to meet the views of the Committee of the Lancashire County Coun- cil as expressed at the above meeting, the Local ority of Widnes on the requisite Parliamentary sanction I being obtained contribute a sum of £30,000 towards the cost of the undertaking on the understanding that Run- corn also contributes £30,000, and that the balance of such cost is provided by the County Councilsof Lanca- shire and Cheshire. The minutes were approved on the motion of Mr. Brown seconded by Mr. Beech.

div.head: CIRENCESTER ELECTION.
div.p: CIRENCESTER ELECTION.

----- Polling commenced in the Cirencester Division of Gloucestershire on Thursday morning for the election of a Parliamentary representative ta fill the vacancy caused by the death of Mr. A. B. Winterbotham. The candi- dates are Colonel Chester Masters (Conservative) and Mr. H. B. W. Lawson (Liberal). The reault will, it is ex- pected, be declared about noon on Friday. At the last general election Mr. Winterbotham was returned by a majority of 153. The weather was most favourable, and polling opened briskly' at the whole of the thirty polling places. The latest card issued by the Liberals runs, "Good morning have you voted for Lawson? You won't be happy till you do." The counting began at eleven o'clock on Friday, and the result was declared as follows : Colonel C. Master (C) • H. L. W. Lawson (L)

LATEST NEWS.

SOUTH AFRICAN EXPERIENCES OF A RUNCORN MISSIONARY. On Thursday evening the Rev. S. H. Havenscroft, a native of the town, delivered a lecture in the St. Paul's Chapel,.Runcorn,on twelve 'rears' experience as a missionary in South Africa. There was a good attendance, and Mr. Robert Shaw, of Mossley-hill, formerly of Runcorn, presided.—The Chairman, in opening the proceedings, said Brunswick Schools had always stood in the forefront of missionary enterprise, and they were permitted that evening to have an experience that few congregations had. They were aßpleased that the Lord twelve years ago put it into the heart of Mr. Ravenscroft to enter into this work—a very important, very difficult, and in slime respects a very dangerous calling—and to which he was about to return. kapplause.) They were proud that one of them—one of their scholars, had been to South. Africa, and was prepared to tell them that the Jesus that had done so much for them was also powerful over the hearts of those in other climes. (Applause.)—ln a short speech the Rev. T. Wilkes said Mr. Ra‘,ens- croft had done a good work in South Africa, The Lecturer,,who was cordially received, described his voyage out to South Africa in the steamship Dunbar, twelve years ago, and then in graphic language pro- ceeded to narrate his experiences amongst the natives. He pourtrayed the habits and customs of the Hottentots and Kaffers,and the difficulties to be surmounted before they could be brought within ti e pale of Christian faith. The greatest enemy of the natives, he said, was drink. At the conclusion, Mr. Ravenscroft exhibited a number of African curios. Short speeches were made by Mr. Robert Norman, and Rev. W. Arrowsmith. On the motion of Mr. P. Speakman seconded by Mr. S. Ravens- croft son, a vote of thanks was accorded to the Chair.- man. The collection in aid of the Rev. S. H..Ravens- croft's missionary work realised £23 14s. Bd..inoludiug, a donation of £lO from Mr. Shaw. DARES B R 57 HIGHWAY: B 0 A RD,..

PUBLIC NOTICE. THE SHOP ASSISTANTS' HALF HOLIDAY has been granted since March 24th by a large majority of tradesmen. but it is remarkable that it is still refused by a few who could well afford to close on Thursday& at one o'clock. It is also being further endangered by the action of one or two lea Dug tradesmen who are contemplating breaking through the arrangement. We hereby strongly appeal to the pubic of Warrington and district to decline to purchase after one o'clock.

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN, that the next GENERAL QUARTER SESSIONS of the Peace for the COUNTY OF CHESTER will be holden at the COURT HOUSE, NETHER KNUTSFORD, in and for the said County, on MONDAY, the 17th day of October next, at half- past eleven o'clock in the Forenoon, when the Grand Jury will be empannelled. The hearing of all appeals arising within the Hundreds of Bucklow. Macclesfield, and Northwich, forming the Knuts- ford District, and the trials of all prisoners committed from such Hundreds, will take. place at such Sessions. The GrAnd and Petty Jury for the Knutsford District must be in atten- dance at the Court House, Hnutsford, at the opening of the Court on MONDAY, the 17th day of October, at Half-past Eleven o'clock in the Forenoon. THE Court will te Adjourned to the Castle of Chester, on THURSDAY, the 20th day of October next, at eleven o'clock in the Forenoon, when another Grand Jury will be empannelled. The hearing of all Appeals arising within the Hundreds of Broxtoti, Eddisbury, Nantwich and Wirral, forming the Chester District, and the trials of all prisoners committed from the last-mentioned Hundreds will take place at such Adjourned Sessions. The Grand and Petty Jury for the Chester District must be in attendance at the Castle of Ches- ter, at the opening of the Court on THURSDAY. the 20.11 day of October next, at Eleven o'clock in the Forenoon. REGINALD POTTS. Clerk of the Peace for the County of Chesty.. Chester, 261 h September, 1892.

KEATING'S COUGH LOZENGES. "94, Commercial Road,Peckham, July 12, 1889. " Dear Sir,—l am a poor hand at expressing my feelings, but I should like to thank you. A FISHIN' "Do." -- Three chaps fro Golborne, not lung sin,' Coom o'er to fish 'i'th bruck ; To try ther ovverpowerin' skill, An' test ther bloomin' luck. One on urn twigg'd me "on the job," An' whisper'd "Neaw owd flick, If theaur't fer publishin' this • do,' Don't dobb it on to thick !" "• Aw reet," aw sed, "but, lost of aw, Go, get a sope to sup; f o looken cowd, an' summut warm 1311 keep yer sperrits up." Well, off they went, an' when they'd done, Sir James remarkt to Dick, "By Gyow, owd mon, we'st noan catch mitch, We'n dobb'd it on to thick I" Heawev er thay rowt th' wayter side, Its not fer me to say; But still they walk'd as if they'd lied A strnnger dose than ray ! They soon aw geet ther tackle eawt, An' wurm'd it double quick; But aw the same, th ay soon fund eawt. They'd dobb'd it on to thick ! One on um, but aw shan't say which, His rod an' line he lost; Wi' hookid wot he thowt a pike, He clutter't in, yed fost ! Then, quick ez thowt, they pond him eawt„ Far nigher deead then wick; Wile, in a murmur he coiefessed, He'd dobb'd it on to thick ! But th' spree—if yo cud caw it spree— Wur not hawf o'er ez yet, That seet th' Angler welly dreawnt, Aw never shall forget. An wen he went to change his togs, An' look'd so pale an' sick, Why, even I wur beaund to own, He'd dobb'd it on to thick! Thoose breeches that he'd getten in, Wur quite a foot to wide; Yo met ha' put another mon I' th' belly-bent's inside An' ez fer th' legs reet tow'rt his knees, They'd march't up dubble quick ; Another proof, if that wur aw, He'd dobb'd it on to thick ! Well, ther's an send o' aw things, lads ; An' so, wen aw wur o'er, They fund they'd catch'd a cowd apiece, An' jack-sharps hauf a score ! So here's a morril to my tale— Th' owd station rnester's pick— " Wene'er yo' goo a fishin', lad', Don't dobb it on to thick !" TUVE 0' PEGS. Nyowton, God bless o' 14, 10, 92.

MURDEIt IN IRELAND OF k FARMER. _- Yesterday morning the body .of Michael Corcoran, of .Glencurra, county Wexford, was found floating off the coast. The deceased attended Waterford fair on the &di inst., and sold eleven heifers for £lO4. He left for home in the evening under the influence of drink, but never reached it. No money was found on the body. • THE • CONGREGATIONAL UNION- AT, BRADFORD. - The concluding gatherings of the autumnal assembly of the Congregational Union of England and Wales were being held in Bradford yesterday, The day's proceed- ings cm-mewed with a breakfast to the local treasurers and secretaries of the London Missimary Society, in the Liberal Club ; and this was followed by a private con- ference- of county union treasurers and secretaries, • presided ever by the Rev. W. F. Clarkson, secretary. of • ChurchoAid Society FAILURE, OF A CHESHIRE- LAND' AGENT. A WARRANT ISSUED. At Crewe Bankruptcy Court, yesterday, Mr. Bullock, - official receiver, reported the disappearance of Richard Edward Speakman., a. bankrupt. At the last examine- - tion debtor was ordered to file certain accounts. Mr. Oooke, his solicitor,, now reed a letter from Montreal, whither the debtor had gone, stating he could not com- ply, with the order. The deficiency is about £5,000, and the debtor admitted betting heavily. A warrant was issued for his arrest. • EXPLOSION IN A COALMINE.. FIVE-LIVES LOST. WILREEBARRE, . PA, FRIDAY.—A fearful explosion through firedamp has taken place at Stirling Colliery. Five miners lost their lives ten were badly burnt, and eight men are shut up•in a:drift. Wilmrsaidartm, Lama,—Two imprisoned men were rescued at 10 o'clock last night. They are in a critical condition, and there is little hope that the remaining six will be taken out alive. • The colliery is operated by the Philadelphia and Reading Coal and Iron Company. RENEWED STORM. FEARED. Funna FLOODS. 'A fearful hurricane is raging along the North Wales coast, the full effects of which are felt at Llandudno and Colwyn Bay, which lieopen to gales from the south-east, as this is. Rain is again falling in torrents in Cheshire, and there is every indication of a renewal of the floods. A very strong gale, accompanied by a heavy sea, pre- vails off the caast of Bedlam and Northumberland, and a number of vessels are detained in Shields Harbour. A +SCHOONER ASHORE. The schooner Isabella, bound for Hull with a cargo of oil, broke from her anchorage off Lowestoft early yeSter- day morning during a heavy northerly gale and drifted ashore. The crew were rescued with a rocket apparatus. • THE WAGES CRISIS IN THE COITON TRADE. Meetings have been held during the past few days of the operative spinners in Stalvbridge, Mossley, Droyla- den, and Ashton, with reference to the proposal to reduce the wages 5 per cent. In each case resolutions were unanimously adopted instructing the delegates at a representative meeting to-morrow (Saturday), to strenuously resist the proposals of the employers. Returns to hand yesterday moraine show that at all twelve meetings of cotton operative held at Oldham on Thursday night-it was:decided to refuse the reduction, and to pay extra levies. At a crowded meeting of the Blackburn Operatives Spinners' Association,on Thursday night, the threatened reduction of wages in the spinning trade was discussed, and it was unanimously decided to imnose an extraor- dinary levy of alt. per man in support of the strike funds of the Northern Counties Amalgamation of Cotton Spinners.
